questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was an esteemed university and that I had friends who had had good experiences being on exchange there.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I ended up enjoying the social and personal aspects of the exchange way more than the academic. I was actually quite disappointed by the quality of the education at the host university.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: what I needed. (what am I supposed to answer to this? - everything that was done? - too much to list)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was my host institution that simply offered me a place. So I don not think it could have been any easier.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I don't think there is any important detail, they won't figure out themselves.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I am okay with mess. We were 170 students with only one (small) industrial-type kitchen. Many of the students were not happy with it, but I can live on a rock, so I didn't care.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is a bit weird at ETH Zürich in that you first register for every and any course you could even just imagine taking and then you turn up to the first two lectures or so to find out if the course fits you and then you de-register from all the courses you find out are not for you. Beware - they courses are not worth a lot of ECTS credits compared to UCPH.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: oops, just did.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Every, I think.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: successful for all the ones they actually ran that semester (but I knew ahead of arriving, that certain courses, I had had my eyes on, were not going to be available for me).

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register for more courses, than you think you will take. (you only de-register from the exams way way later - so there is pretty much no risk). ALSO, check whether the exam is a "session exam" or a "end-of-semester exam". The "session exams" are in August.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: One of the courses I took was one of the best courses I have ever taken and two others were also pretty good, but the last two courses I took were, by far, the worst taught courses I have ever taken.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Mainly master courses - but I was also mainly taking master courses at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different from course to course. Some very different and some basically exactly the same.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Algebraic Geometry
Graph Theory
Morse Homology
Riemann Surfaces
Topology of Manifolds

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Topology of Manifolds was one of the best courses I have ever taken. D. Cekic is one of the very best lecturers I have ever had! - an absolute joy!
Graph Theory and Riemann Surfaces were completely fine courses, pretty good actually.
The "lectures" in Algebraic Geometry were 125 YouTube videos ... bad videos even.
Half of the time, the lecturer in Morse Homology did not even understand themselves what was going on.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Buying a Wifi-router. Bouldering membership was more expensive than expected.

Also I just bought a cheap bike and biked pretty much anywhere in any weather up and down hills so that was way cheaper than paying for public transport.

I had EU insurance, if I had not had that, it would have been quite expensive. I also had a cheap data subscription for like 60 DKK a month.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: pretty much everything was more expensive than I expected except for groceries and especially tofu was cheap. Anything that is not groceries is extremely expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Fantastic climbing gym "Minimum boulders" - just quite expensive.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: ASVZ is a fantastic free place to get instructions in all kinds of sports with really nice facilities! There were also some activities arranged by the student clubs and ESN Zürich (but not that many by ESN).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Bouldering, going to see some of the experimental theatre and some concerts.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Hiking, bouldering, swimming, Skiing, national parades and festivals. - so much to do!
possibly clubbing, but the clubs are more like high-school parties

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very. Zürich is very similar to Copenhagen.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: not really - I didn't do it much. It is quite difficult. I just socialized with the students at my housing, since there were plenty all the time.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: arrogance and the very strict rule-following. But this was still fine.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That things for the most part just worked and people were friendly once you initiated the conversation.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Use some of all the opportunities you are given there.
Spend energy on actively being social in the beginning.
Enjoy Switzerland while you are there (there will probably be a lot of stress when it comes to courses - maybe choose some easier courses).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I have probably forgotten something important.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many new friends and just growing as a person (have already had some of them visit me here in Copenhagen).

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: In the beginning I was not that social.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I have definitely forgotten something important but I really just need to finish this now.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
